correctness.rationale: The quotient algebra is exactly the published lower-triangular algebra. Compressing any ideal element by the diagonal idempotents isolates each nonzero scalar coordinate. A nonzero first coordinate forces the first idempotent and hence the whole radical into the ideal; a nonzero second coordinate does the symmetric thing; both coordinates force the unit. If both diagonal coordinates vanish, two-sided multiplication acts on the radical only by scalars, so every and only closed linear subspaces occur. Quotient correspondence then transfers the exhaustive list to closed ideals containing the compacts. The identification of the radical preimage with the inessential ideal is explicitly published.

value.rationale: Closed-ideal lattices of operator algebras are a central structural invariant, and the focal realization creates a new family parameterized by arbitrary separable coefficient spaces. Completing the interval result to an exhaustive classification above the compacts is natural: it identifies the only two maximal ideals, their exact intersection, and shows that all remaining complexity is exactly the closed-subspace lattice of the prescribed dual radical. This extends the finite diamond phenomenon of the earlier Kania--Laustsen construction to arbitrary dual radicals rather than selecting an ad hoc subspace or recomputing a known table.
